A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same token-discarding and Token Spuriosity Index study despite the changed title. All supplied pages, including v2 Appendices A–E, are readable, and shared methods, tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments with supervised, DINO and MAE models, attribution comparisons, and a VinDR-Mammo case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original noise-perturbation comparisons and segmentation-mask analyses.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3.3.1 defines token influence as the absolute confidence change; v2 Definition 1 uses the signed confidence decrease. This changes the specified scoring component, while individual-token removal and the two TSI ratio structures remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation or retained experiments were updated accordingly.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a selective core-versus-non-core Gaussian-corruption scenario using 4,375 annotated images from 20 classes. The original ImageNet classification and mammography coverage remain. The segmentation analysis uses existing ImageNet validation images and does not introduce a segmentation prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 adds the mask-based Gaussian-perturbation comparator NSI and directly compares it with TSI in Figure 13 and Table 6. The existing GradCAM and attention-map comparisons are retained, mainly in Appendix C.

E3.justification: Two additional evaluation designs are introduced: core/non-core perturbations with Gaussian noise of sigma 0.25 and threshold-based TSI–NSI agreement, and paired bounding-box versus segmentation-mask scoring on 7,117 correctly classified images. The original ImageNet partitions, ViT-B/16 configuration and token-removal budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds validation against a different feature-importance mechanism. Section 4 and Appendix D add annotation-granularity sensitivity analysis, paired score-difference distributions and annotation-inconsistency examples. Earlier GradCAM, attention-proxy and TSI-correlation analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The existing mean/standard-deviation summaries, Pearson correlations and R-squared reporting remain. New analyses add agreement percentages and distributions, but neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 6 newly reports A-TSI/NSI agreement of 59.5%, 79.5% and 65.8% for supervised, DINO and MAE models. Figure 16 adds the finding that segmentation masks generally increase M-TSI and decrease A-TSI. All six original tables retain their numerical values after matching, while one qualitative example from v1 Figure 8 is omitted.

T1.justification: v2 adds a Shapley-value decomposition and weighted-surrogate interpretation, together with claimed leave-one-out attribution properties. It also revises the formal influence definition from absolute to signed change and defines NSI mathematically in Appendix C.3. These extend the mathematical content beyond v1's influence definition and two TSI ratios; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the method's novelty by explicitly positioning it as a diagnostic pipeline using standard leave-one-out removal. Its abstract drops the promise of an exhaustive image list and associated cautionary-use recommendation. The central contributions concerning TSI, training-method dependence and recurring ImageNet artifacts remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes reliance outside annotations from genuinely spurious features and acknowledges the absence of ground-truth spuriosity validation. Appendix C.5 strengthens attention-map limitations through specific discussion of information mixing and outlier tokens. New interpretations explain perturbation disagreements and how annotation granularity affects the two metrics.

D1.justification: v2 adds annotation provenance, including ILSVRC localization boxes and Gao et al.'s segmentation annotations, plus noise-construction details for the new comparison. Conversely, v1's specification that attention maps use the final-layer CLS token is omitted. This omission does not establish an actual change of attention layer.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning within removal-based explanation, occlusion and Shapley-related research, adding discussions of Li et al., Covert et al., and Lundberg and Lee, among others. The method is explicitly framed as adapting established leave-one-out attribution to token removal. v1's specific analogy to Madsen et al. is removed.

P1.justification: The title changes and the narrative is substantially reorganized: method exposition precedes datasets/models, the medical case and metric selection become standalone sections, and numerous analyses move into appendices. Related work, method explanations and conclusions are extensively rewritten. The medical-image description is corrected from MRI to mammography.

P2.justification: The body changes from two columns to a single-column layout. Retained TSI and correlation tables are restructured, several figures are rearranged or relocated, and v1 Figure 8 is reduced from four examples to three. New segmentation illustrations, NSI comparison plots and score-difference histograms substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful cross-method and annotation-sensitivity evidence and more explicit limitations. However, Definition 1 replaces absolute influence with signed influence without explaining negative contributions or reconciling the change with unchanged TSI interpretations and retained numerical results. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an intended implementation change or a documentation error. That uncertainty concerns the central diagnostic score, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
